prompt:
A loose ink-wash painting on one plain sheet of warm, light rice paper with fine fibres, seen flat from straight above, evenly lit, no shadow, no frame, no table, no text, no letters, no numbers, no signature, no red seal, no stamp. Paint it the way a master ink painter works: a few confident, loose brush strokes, wet ink bleeding softly into the paper, dry-brush texture where the brush runs out, simplified forms that suggest rather than describe, lots of white paper. It must look like a painting, expressive and artistic, with the brushwork of the reference picture: never a realistic drawing, never a detailed illustration, never a pencil sketch, never a 3D render, never a photograph. Copy only the reference's brushwork, never its subject: no bird, no crane, no reeds. Only the things named below are painted: no mountains, no pine trees, no buildings, no people, no extra plants or objects, nothing Asian in style or subject (no pagodas, no lanterns, no characters, no bamboo, no plum blossom). Sumi ink from deep black to soft grey washes, soft watercolour only where a colour is named, and real gold leaf only where stated. Generous empty paper on every side. The subject fills most of the picture (about 85% of its height and width): bold, generous, never small in the middle of empty paper.

One single long sugar pine cone from the Sierra Nevada, lying diagonally across the picture and filling it, seen from the side. Its many overlapping scales are painted in quick, confident dry-brush strokes of warm brown and grey ink, each scale one or two touches, darker where they overlap, with paper showing through between them; the cone is loose and expressive, never a detailed botanical drawing. A short piece of stem at its top end. On three or four scale tips, a tiny drop of clear resin painted as a small bead of real gold leaf. A faint soft grey shadow under the cone. Nothing else: no branch, no needles, no tree, no ground. Calm, natural, complete.
